headline: An Indian start-up has shown a full-size model of a planned AI-piloted combat drone, but nothing has flown and no government order has been confirmed.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: unveiled 13 Oct 2026 as a static prototype, with performance only as design targets and no contract.
importance_line: It points to India's interest in cheap AI-piloted wingmen for fighters, but the aircraft has not flown and its figures are the company's targets.
summary: Army Recognition reports that Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace, a Bengaluru start-up founded in 2022, showed a full-size static prototype of the FWD Supreme in New Delhi on 13 Oct 2026, billed as India's first home-built AI-driven combat drone. Its range, payload and speed are design targets only, the smaller demonstrator has completed ground taxi trials but not flown, and no government contract or funding has been confirmed.
notes: Counts toward robot war limit (military drone).
